describes: Each part as a family of versions, each made in its years (`years`, the year the part was made: the house's building, or the event that renewed it), by those who could pay for it (`wealth`), and how often it was chosen (`weight`). The house's seed picks one per family from those its facts allow; every opening of one making shares it. Shared by every era: a version naming `eras` is made only for houses of those eras; one without is any house's, as a later replacement is.

casing.describes: A flat board with a bead run on its edge at the opening: the plain house's casing.
An empire casing: a raised fillet along its outer edge falling in an ovolo to the flat, so a line of shadow rings the opening.
A plain planed board with its arrises eased: the later and the cheap casing (a shed's door, a modern window).
System 2's side board (Heng 2015): about 122 mm wide and 25 thick, two flutes run down it; the upper block sits on its top.

head.describes: A frieze board under a sloped cap with a bed mould: the classical cornice over every opening (photo 09).
A plain sloped water board, no bed mould, less proud.
A plain head board with a thin sloped cap, no bed mould.
System 2's head (Heng 2015): a block on each side board's top under a water board sloped 20 degrees with a cove under its edge, the frieze between about 250 mm from the frame.

sill.describes: A thick sloped sill with horns past the casing.
System 2's sill (Heng 2015): the lower water board on two ogee brackets about 230 mm long and 60 thick, one under each side board.

window.describes: Two side-hung casements, three panes each, either side of a post: the empire window (wooden-town-architecture.md; ref 07, 02). Outward-opening, its panes puttied from outside: a bar shows a thin ridge of wood between two slopes of putty. Its joinery as made (mm): frameMm the frame's face and depth, coverMm what the casing laps of its outer edge, lapMm what each sash laps of the frame's rebate and the post; sashMm and barMm the sightlines (stile and rail, bar), the putty or bead inside them; the frame shows frameMm - coverMm - lapMm, the post postMm - 2 lapMm. Checked by the glass's share across the opening against the reference's (house.json glassAcross).

Two casements, two panes each, either side of a post: the later classical window, its panes bigger as cylinder glass came in bigger sheets. Its joinery as made (mm): frameMm the frame's face and depth, coverMm what the casing laps of its outer edge, lapMm what each sash laps of the frame's rebate and the post; sashMm and barMm the sightlines (stile and rail, bar), the putty or bead inside them; the frame shows frameMm - coverMm - lapMm, the post postMm - 2 lapMm. Checked by the glass's share across the opening against the reference's (house.json glassAcross).

The sveitser cross-post window (krysspost): a post and a transom, a top light each side over the transom, and under it two casements with a bar across each, six lights (wooden-town-architecture.md; ref 05). Factory joinery from the 1880s (Bjorheim from 1882), set into old openings when older houses were updated. Its joinery as made (mm): frameMm the frame's face and depth, coverMm what the casing laps of its outer edge, lapMm what each sash laps of the frame's rebate and the post; sashMm and barMm the sightlines (stile and rail, bar), the putty or bead inside them; the frame shows frameMm - coverMm - lapMm, the post postMm - 2 lapMm. Checked by the glass's share across the opening against the reference's (house.json glassAcross).

The 1960s window set into an old opening (house-changes.md; ref 10, 04): one plain casement, one big sealed double pane held by flat beads, no post and no bars; the opening kept, so the pane is as tall as the old window. Its joinery as made (mm): frameMm the frame's face and depth, coverMm what the casing laps of its outer edge, lapMm what each sash laps of the frame's rebate and the post; sashMm and barMm the sightlines (stile and rail, bar), the putty or bead inside them; the frame shows frameMm - coverMm - lapMm, the post postMm - 2 lapMm. Checked by the glass's share across the opening against the reference's (house.json glassAcross).

door.describes: A pair of tall raised panels under a three-light top light.

eave.describes: The classical eave: a short soffit closed by a fascia, 140 mm out.

chimney.describes: A brick stack under render, its top corbelled out by two courses, a short crown above.
A rendered stack with a projecting band two courses under its top.
A plain rendered stack, its top chamfered: a later stack, or one rebuilt, without the old corbelled top.

roof.describes: Single-S red pantiles from Sandnes Teglverk.
